messages:
maya: PR 49821 is ready for merge — it adjusts KV eviction thresholds and adds a fallback routing policy for overloaded hosts. Please sign off: runtime, platform, security. No schema changes, no user-facing contract changes. Link: https://git.internal/r/redwood/pr/49821

samir: quick q — what's the expected perf delta in peak qps? do we need a different canary size?

maya: perf delta is ~+3% tail in our internal sysbench on p4; median unchanged. plan is 1% traffic for 30m, then 10% for 1h if stable.

olga: can you paste the rollback plan? who watches the canary dashboards?

maya: rollback plan = revert to commit c4f3b2 if errors >1% or latency spike >200ms p95. I'll own monitoring during canary (will mute alerts I own). ops-oncall and runtime team as backup.

jordan: heads-up — this touches KMS policy for cache encryption? any new keys or IAM changes? I can do a quick audit.

maya: no new keys, just a KMS key usage flag flip for existing key (no policy edits). I added the config diff in the PR description.

ci-bot: CI pipeline: unit ✓, integration ✓, e2e ✓, security-scan ✓ — all green (build 49821.3).

samir: looks fine to me from runtime side; small nit in test naming but not blocking. runtime +1 (will +lgtm on green).

olga: platform +1 after you share the canary dashboard links in the PR. need to know which metrics to watch (evictions, queue length, error-rate).

maya: added dashboard link to PR and listed the three metrics (evictions/sec, request_queue_len, error_rate_5m).

jordan: ran quick config check — no IAM changes required. security +1, recommend follow-up audit note in the changelog.

samir: can someone trigger the merge when the canary window starts? I can shepherd the rollout at 13:00 PT.

maya: I can merge at 13:00 PT and start the canary, pinging runtime oncall.

olga: ack — I'll stand by to abort if platform thresholds cross. :thumbsup:

samir: thanks all — will monitor logs for the first 15m. ping here if anything odd.

maya: thanks — merging at 13:00 PT unless anyone objects. :rocket:
